CLIMATE NOTE

NOTE
No significant weather expected today while a jet max ejects across The UP and into Ontario. The occluded low pressure system stemming from this wave exhibits vertical continuity through the 300 mb level while the progressive surface reflection tracks from The Northwest Angle to James Bay between 12Z and 00Z today. Meanwhile, lower tropospheric theta-e advection begins to work into Southeast Michigan from the confluent southwesterly trajectories. The latest NCEP solutions continue to resolve nil QPF given the lack of precipitation response upon arrival of the system's cold front. The front is still expected to transition to a stationary boundary over Lower Michigan, and will be met with ambient dryness through much of the atmospheric column. A representative sampling of area forecast soundings indicates broad dewpoint depressions and established static stability between the 5 kft and 15 kft AGL layers, attributed to the distant influence of Mid-Atlantic mid level ridging. PWATs will rise, marked by the present increase in high cloud fraction and an attempt later today at some component of diurnal cumuliform cloud. Compared to the 19.00Z KDTX RAOB, PWATs increase by a factor of three this afternoon, from 0.22 to around 0.60 inches. However, the lack of saturation precludes any potential for rain. Main forecast concern today remains focused on southwesterly wind magnitudes as the CWA becomes positioned between strengthening gradient flow from the low to the northwest and surface high pressure to the southeast. As discussed over the last several forecast cycles, the shallow mixing depths will limit the frequency and duration of peak gusts today. The strongest low level jet winds should reside farther north with closer proximity to slightly cooler air. Areas north of M-46 stand the best chance to see gusts of 30+ mph this afternoon while gusts should generally hold below 25 mph toward the south. Ridging returns Friday with dry weather persisting into the weekend. Any westerly component to area winds drops off as the day progresses, backing southerly by the afternoon hours as the surface anticyclone recenters over central Appalachia. Upstream, a Pacific longwave trough works through the Four Corners area before gradually phasing with a meandering upper low moving south across the Canadian Prairies. As this unfolds, the eastern CONUS jet will strengthen, although split-flow should reside over/near Southeast Michigan into Saturday. Double digit 850 mb temperatures are becoming more likely on Saturday resulting in widespread highs within the low to mid 60s. The next chance for rain comes Sunday as the composite trough axis releases across the Midwest. Latest medium range solutions have shown signs of deamplification upon reaching the Great Lakes, but the baroclinic zone and kinematics favor a period of showers on Sunday. Turning much colder post-frontal Monday with an arctic airmass spilling in from 1040 mb Saskatchewan/Manitoba high pressure. Wind chills drop into the teens at times. && .MARINE... A stacked low pressure system over far southwestern Ontario this morning will track northeast reaching James Bay by this evening. While it tracks through Ontario, the gradient between the low and the ridge over the East Coast will tighten across the Great Lakes. The increased southwesterly flow funneling out of Saginaw Bay will lead to a period of wind gusts near 25 knots tonight through Thursday evening. A small craft advisory has been issued. Ridging will build back into the state tonight and Friday leading to lighter winds with peak speeds largely under 15 knots. The next trough will approach the region Saturday leading to increasing southwesterly flow ahead of the trough. A cold front will then drop through the region Sunday night leading to stronger northwesterly flow and a cold airmass dropping across the lakes. && .PREV DISCUSSION... Issued at 1129 PM EST Wed Nov 18 2026 AVIATION... Ample dry air associated with the large high pressure system centered over the eastern US will maintain clear skies below 20k feet through Thurs morning. The combination of extremely dry surface air and the persistence of a light south-southwest gradient will inhibit early morning fog development. Southwest winds will increase Thurs afternoon as the gradient flow increases, supporting wind gusts at or above 20 knots. For DTW...Light south winds and very dry air will inhibit any impactful concerns to aviation Thursday. DTW THRESHOLD PROBABILITIES... * None. && .DTX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES... MI...None. Lake Huron...Small Craft Advisory until 10 PM EST this evening for LHZ421-441. Lake St Clair...None. .DISCUSSION...

No significant weather expected today while a jet max ejects across 
The UP and into Ontario. The occluded low pressure system stemming 
from this wave exhibits vertical continuity through the 300 mb level 
while the progressive surface reflection tracks from The Northwest 
Angle to James Bay between 12Z and 00Z today. Meanwhile, lower 
tropospheric theta-e advection begins to work into Southeast 
Michigan from the confluent southwesterly trajectories. The latest 
NCEP solutions continue to resolve nil QPF given the lack of 
precipitation response upon arrival of the system's cold front. The 
front is still expected to transition to a stationary boundary over 
Lower Michigan, and will be met with ambient dryness through much of 
the atmospheric column. A representative sampling of area forecast 
soundings indicates broad dewpoint depressions and established 
static stability between the 5 kft and 15 kft AGL layers, attributed 
to the distant influence of Mid-Atlantic mid level ridging. PWATs 
will rise, marked by the present increase in high cloud fraction and 
an attempt later today at some component of diurnal cumuliform 
cloud. Compared to the 19.00Z KDTX RAOB, PWATs increase by a factor 
of three this afternoon, from 0.22 to around 0.60 inches. However, 
the lack of saturation precludes any potential for rain.

Main forecast concern today remains focused on southwesterly wind 
magnitudes as the CWA becomes positioned between strengthening 
gradient flow from the low to the northwest and surface high 
pressure to the southeast. As discussed over the last several 
forecast cycles, the shallow mixing depths will limit the frequency 
and duration of peak gusts today. The strongest low level jet winds 
should reside farther north with closer proximity to slightly cooler 
air. Areas north of M-46 stand the best chance to see gusts of 30+ 
mph this afternoon while gusts should generally hold below 25 mph 
toward the south.

Ridging returns Friday with dry weather persisting into the weekend. 
Any westerly component to area winds drops off as the day 
progresses, backing southerly by the afternoon hours as the surface 
anticyclone recenters over central Appalachia. Upstream, a Pacific 
longwave trough works through the Four Corners area before gradually 
phasing with a meandering upper low moving south across the Canadian 
Prairies. As this unfolds, the eastern CONUS jet will strengthen, 
although split-flow should reside over/near Southeast Michigan into 
Saturday. Double digit 850 mb temperatures are becoming more likely 
on Saturday resulting in widespread highs within the low to mid 60s. 
The next chance for rain comes Sunday as the composite trough axis 
releases across the Midwest. Latest medium range solutions have 
shown signs of deamplification upon reaching the Great Lakes, but 
the baroclinic zone and kinematics favor a period of showers on 
Sunday. Turning much colder post-frontal Monday with an arctic 
airmass spilling in from 1040 mb Saskatchewan/Manitoba high 
pressure. Wind chills drop into the teens at times.

.MARINE...

A stacked low pressure system over far southwestern Ontario this 
morning will track northeast reaching James Bay by this evening. 
While it tracks through Ontario, the gradient between the low and 
the ridge over the East Coast will tighten across the Great Lakes. 
The increased southwesterly flow funneling out of Saginaw Bay will 
lead to a period of wind gusts near 25 knots tonight through 
Thursday evening. A small craft advisory has been issued. Ridging 
will build back into the state tonight and Friday leading to lighter 
winds with peak speeds largely under 15 knots. The next trough will 
approach the region Saturday leading to increasing southwesterly 
flow ahead of the trough. A cold front will then drop through the 
region Sunday night leading to stronger northwesterly flow and a 
cold airmass dropping across the lakes.
